card.name: Modifier word before a noun phrase
card.fires_on: An adjective or modifier such as "strong", "very" or "fact" that sits right before a noun and is followed by a CYP enzyme term or a similar noun. It is most common in instructions to resume a dose after a strong CYP3A inhibitor or inducer is stopped.

modes.label: Strong before CYP inhibitor
modes.description: The word "strong" just before CYP3A inhibitor or inducer, in dose-resumption instructions.
modes.example: resume the ZELBORAF dose that was taken prior to initiating the<< strong>> CYP3A4 inducer.

modes.label: Other modifiers before a noun
modes.description: Words like "very", "fact" or "troubled" that modify the next noun in a set phrase.
modes.example: moderately preterm (32-36 weeks) and<< very>> preterm (<32 weeks).

card.plain: It fires on a describing word, usually "strong", that comes just before the noun it describes, such as a CYP3A inhibitor.
